final_answer:
DEVIATION REPORT - VOLTA ESLA-2025-0512-GD v. GREENFIELD PLAYBOOK v4.0 (PRIVILEGED / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT)
To: M. Calloway (GC); cc D. Sung, P. Ramanathan. From: Birchwood & Hale LLP.

1. BASIS AND BOTTOM LINE
Reviewed: Volta draft ESLA (body, Exhibits A-D), Playbook v4.0 (Jan. 15, 2025), and the Apr. 28-May 3, 2025 internal email chain. No external law was researched; the benchmark is the Playbook, which binds outside counsel.
Tier 1 applies (license fees $22.35M + $1.275M implementation = $23.625M; threshold $2M). Because TCV exceeds $10M, Board Audit Committee reporting/approval is required. Any Red Line concession needs the GC's prior written waiver and risk assessment before it is communicated to Volta (Playbook 1, 2.2).
Result: the draft is a vendor form that hits 18 Red Lines, including all four Derek Sung must-win items. Signing as drafted is not possible without GC waivers we do not recommend. Only payment terms, Named User model, confidentiality term and the Licensee-side cure mechanics are within Playbook ranges.
Severity key: CRITICAL = Sung must-win item (and Red Line); HIGH = Red Line; MEDIUM = outside Acceptable Range, not Red Line; LOW = minor or not Playbook-covered.

2. SUMMARY TABLE
(ESLA section | Draft | Playbook | Severity)
1. Data use, 6.1, 11.5, 12.2 | Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, survives termination license to aggregated/anonymized Licensee Data for product development, benchmarking and ML/AI training; no consent | 6.1: no ML/AI training in any form; any aggregated use only with prior written consent; perpetual/irrevocable license is Red Line (three Red Lines) | CRITICAL
2. Customization IP, 1.7, 5.2, 5.3 | Volta solely owns all Customizations, including Greenfield-built ones using its specs; Greenfield "hereby assigns"; Greenfield's use ends at expiry; Feedback assigned | 5.1: Licensee owns; Volta gets only a "generalized learnings" license; ownership and use survive termination. Assignment and post-termination loss of use are each Red Lines | CRITICAL
3. Escrow, 7 | No escrow; discretionary negotiation of a separate agreement at extra cost | 4.4: mandatory independent escrow for on-premise code (6 sites); triggers: insolvency, 60-day uncured material breach, cessation of support, successor discontinuance; Licensee release license; cost under $25K/yr to Licensee. Red Line | CRITICAL
4. Termination for convenience, 11.2, 11.4 | Volta may terminate on 60 days without cause; Greenfield has none, renewal included | 9.1: Licensee right required (Acceptable: after year 1, 90 days' notice, fee capped); asymmetry is Red Line | CRITICAL
5. Assignment, 13.5, 2.1 | Mutual consent (not unreasonably withheld); no M&A carve-out; license "non-transferable" and "personal" | 10.1: free assignment on merger, acquisition, reorganization, asset sale; consent for M&A is Red Line | CRITICAL
6. Fees, 3.4, Ex. B 1, 5, 6 | Fixed schedule: +5.1%, +4.8%, +9.2%, +8.4%; no index; renewal up to +12%, then list | 3.1: CPI-U capped at 3% (Preferred) or 4% (Acceptable); any year over 5%, or non-indexed above 4%, is Red Line | HIGH
7. License grant, 2.1, 2.4 | "Access and use" of object code; no modification or derivative works of configuration files/APIs; copies for backup only | 4.1: use, copy, modify for integration, derive configuration files; "access only" for on-premise is Red Line | HIGH
8. Affiliates, 1.4, 2.1 | Licensee employees only; Affiliates need separate agreements and fees | 4.2: Affiliate use required; separate fees Red Line | HIGH
9. Data portability, 6.3 | Proprietary .vdx format, 30 days, then deletion | 6.2: CSV/JSON/XML, no charge, 180 days preferred (90 acceptable); under 60 days or proprietary is Red Line | HIGH
10. Uptime, 8.2, Ex. C 1-3 | 99.5% "commercially reasonable efforts" target; Volta-measured, conclusive; exclusions for emergency maintenance, force majeure, Cascadia/third parties, beta; 24-hour notice, no maintenance cap | 7.1: 99.9% minimum; 4 hrs/month scheduled maintenance, 72 hrs' notice; no other exclusions. All are Red Lines | HIGH
11. Credits, 8.3, Ex. C 4-6 | 2% per full 1% below target, 10% cap, sole and exclusive remedy, 30-day claim, no carryover; no termination right | 7.2: at least 5% per 0.1%; termination for persistent failure; sole remedy Red Line | HIGH
12. IP indemnity, 9.1 | US patent/copyright only; carve-outs for Licensee specs/data and open source; capped at 1x fees actually paid; Volta may terminate and refund current-year fees | 8.1: add trade secret/trademark; uncapped; only three carve-outs. Each is Red Line | HIGH
13. Liability, 10.1-10.2 | Cap (fees "actually paid," 12 months) protects Volta only; Licensee payment and confidentiality/use liability uncapped; no Volta carve-outs; broad consequential waiver (lost data, business interruption, substitute cost) | 8.2: mutual 2x paid or payable (~$7.9M at Year 1); carve-outs for IP indemnity, data breach, gross negligence/willful misconduct, confidentiality, data misuse. Asymmetry, "actually paid," missing carve-outs are Red Lines | HIGH
14. Wind-down, 11.4 | Immediate cessation; uninstall and officer certification in 10 business days | 9.3: 180 days (90 acceptable) at no charge. Red Line, and conflicts with 12.1 | HIGH
15. Transition, 12.1-12.2 | 30 days, on request 15 days before termination, at $375/hr; no successor-vendor cooperation | 9.4: 180 days, free, successor cooperation (below 90 days, charges, no cooperation are Red Lines) | HIGH
16. Law and disputes, 14.1-14.2 | Texas law; JAMS; Austin seat | 10.3: Delaware (Michigan/California acceptable); AAA, Chicago. All three are Red Lines | HIGH
17. Audit, 15.3 | Volta audits "at any time and from time to time" on 10 business days' notice; list-price retroactive true-up plus 18% interest; no Greenfield audit right | 10.4: once a year, 45-60 days' notice; Licensee security/SLA audit right. Notice, frequency and missing right are Red Lines | HIGH
18. Insurance, 16.2 | CGL $2M/$4M; E&O $5M; no cyber, no workers' compensation; no tail; certificates on request; additional insured only to extent of indemnity | 11.1: CGL $5M; E&O $10M; cyber $10M; tail 2-3 yrs; certificates within 30 days. Each shortfall is Red Line (a covenant to maintain exists, so the "representation only" Red Line is not triggered) | HIGH
19. Cure period, 11.3 | 30 days all breaches; mutual | 9.2: 30 monetary / 60 non-monetary preferred, 45-60 acceptable; 30 days meets the Red Line floor but not Acceptable Range | MEDIUM
20. Implementation, 3.2, 4.1 | $1.275M fixed, 50% on signing, non-refundable; no acceptance criteria; Go-Live "target only" yet fees and term run from July 1, 2025 | 3.2: milestone payments tied to objective acceptance preferred; fixed fee itself is permitted | MEDIUM
21. Confidentiality, 13.1 | Mutual; 3 years post-termination; trade secrets indefinitely | 10.2: 5 yrs preferred; 3 is minimum acceptable | LOW
22. Payment, Named Users, 3.3, 2.3 | Net 30; 500 Named Users, quarterly reassignment | 3.2, 4.3: Acceptable. Confirm 500 seats suffice and contractors are permitted | None/LOW

3. KEY ANALYSIS AND RECOMMENDED REDLINES
Priority 1 (Data). Section 6.1 gives with one hand and takes with the other: Greenfield "retains" ownership, but the second paragraph grants Volta an irrevocable perpetual license for ML/AI training with no consent. Section 17.1 (entire agreement) extinguishes Carlos Medina's oral "full data ownership" assurances, so everything must be written. Redline: delete the license; use strictly limited to performing services; no aggregated, anonymized or derived use or ML/AI training without Greenfield's prior written consent in its sole discretion (note: the Playbook treats ML/AI training as Red Line even with consent, so Mr. Sung's email, which would permit use with consent, should be tightened); delete the 6.1 survival reference in 11.5 and the retention language in 12.2. Add breach-notice, security audit and data-breach liability terms, and make any DPA (6.4) negotiated rather than Volta's "then-current" form.
Priority 2 (Customizations). Section 5.2 captures work built from Greenfield's PLC firmware specifications and its trade secrets. The inconsistent restrictions in 2.1/2.4 would also make Greenfield's planned integration work a breach. Redline: Licensee owns all Customizations it creates or that use its data/specifications (Acceptable fallback: joint ownership, but Greenfield sole owner of PLC/sensor integration code); Volta gets a non-exclusive generalized-learnings license; delete assignment and Feedback assignment; ownership and use survive. If Volta will not move, Playbook 5.1 requires immediate GC escalation.
Priority 3 (Escrow). Replace Section 7 with a three-party escrow with Thornbury & Associates (or equivalent), full deposits (source, build scripts, dependencies), updates at each major release, the four triggers, and a perpetual maintenance license on release. Escrow also supports the termination and transition position because the platform runs production lines at six sites.
Priority 4 (Termination/assignment). Section 11.2 lets Volta exit on 60 days; combined with 11.4 (immediate cessation), 5.1/2.1 (no post-termination rights), and no escrow, Volta can stop 24/7 production capability and, at any change of control or assignment request, extract fees. Redline: delete 11.2; add Licensee convenience termination (target: any time on 60 days; fallback: after first anniversary on 90 days, fee capped at the lesser of 50% of remaining current-year fees or one year's fee; no Volta termination except for uncured material breach and insolvency). Section 13.5: Greenfield may assign without consent to a successor in any merger, acquisition, reorganization or asset sale, with post-closing notice only; no fee re-opener or change-of-control termination; make 2.1 "non-transferable/personal" subject to this and extend to Affiliates and successors. Whether a reverse triangular merger is an "assignment" under Texas law (the draft's governing law) was not researched; the contract should resolve it expressly. Present this as a standard Playbook requirement. Per GC instruction, nothing about the confidential acquisition process may be disclosed to Volta.

4. CROSS-CUTTING POINTS
- Integrated continuity failure: 11.4 (cease use immediately) contradicts 12.1 (30-day transition); a 15-day advance request cannot be given for a termination effective immediately; .vdx export, no successor cooperation and no escrow compound it. Playbook 9.3/9.4/6.2/4.4 must be negotiated as a package.
- Section 8.3 (no credit until 98.5%, "per full 1%") conflicts with Exhibit C (2% from below 99.5%); under 17.10 the body controls. Also support is business hours Central only (8.4), though sites run 24/7; SLA excludes on-premise.
- Fee math: Volta schedule totals $22.35M; a 4% cap from Year 2 yields about $21.39M (about $0.96M less); Preferred (fixed through Year 2, then 3%) about $20.48M (about $1.87M less). Year 5 fee $5.15M vs $4.62M.
- Other items not in the Playbook: 1.5%-per-month (18% annual) late interest plus collection costs (3.3); tax gross-up (3.5); Licensee's broad indemnity (9.2(c)) is effectively uncapped; license "subject to timely payment" (2.1); AUP unilaterally amendable (1.1) with immediate suspension (Ex. D 3) and a ban on benchmarking and "competing" development; Upgrades at extra cost and no v8.2 end-of-life protection (4.3); 90-day warranty and "as is" disclaimer (16.1); Volta publicity/logo use without consent (13.3) - consider SEC/Reg FD sensitivity of Greenfield, a NASDAQ issuer; non-solicit (13.4); Effective Date of May 5, 2025 predates signature (June 1 target) and hardcoded 2025 dates need updating if the timetable has slipped.

5. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS
Return a full markup built on the Preferred positions with the Acceptable Range as pre-approved fallbacks (documenting rationale per 1); withhold any Red Line concession pending GC waiver; schedule CTO technical call on integration scope and 24/7 support; calendar Board Audit Committee reporting before the June 1 target; obtain Volta's proof of insurance and escrow-agent preference.
